facts: BARK guided FY2027 revenue of $325–340 million (down from $394.8M in FY26) and adjusted EBITDA of $7–10 million, a meaningful step-up from FY26's $0.2M, with Q1 FY27 revenue guided to $77–79M and EBITDA of $0–1M.
The Board authorized a $40 million share repurchase program to be funded by ongoing free cash flow, the first such program signaling confidence at current stock levels.

Full-year FY26 revenue declined to $394.8M from $484.2M, with Q4 revenue of $86.6M versus $115.4M prior year, reflecting a deliberate $24M+ year-over-year cut in marketing spend (FY26 marketing was $59.2M).
Management is sunsetting the Kibble and toppers product lines due to inadequate returns, reallocating capital to higher-return categories to simplify the business and improve profitability.

D2C revenue is expected to decline year-over-year in 1H FY27 before stabilizing in 2H and returning to growth, as the company enters FY27 with a smaller but higher-quality subscriber base showing improved retention and AOV (D2C gross margin rose 200+ bps to 68%).
Commerce and BARK Air are expected to collectively exceed $100M in FY27 revenue, with Commerce alone projected to grow to roughly 25% of total revenue versus 18% in FY26.

Q4 Commerce revenue fell 18.3% year-over-year to $12.5M due to timing of retail shipments, though full-year Commerce grew modestly to $59.9M (Matt cited $70M including a different segmentation).

The company ended FY26 debt-free with $19M cash and $75.5M inventory (down ~$13M YoY), and expects an additional $12.1M in IEEPA tariff refunds ($7.1M tied to FY26 COGS, $5M to FY27) to be recognized once eligible.
BARK diversified its toy supply chain away from near-total China reliance into multiple Southeast Asian countries and South America, enabling rapid failover if new China tariffs emerge.

Koppers conditionally decided to wind down production at its Stickney, Illinois CM&C facility (impacting ~85 employees), targeting ceased distillation by end of 2026 and shifting production to Nyborg, Denmark in Q4 2026.

The Stickney closure is expected to generate annualized adjusted EBITDA savings of $15M-$20M starting in 2027 (a 75-100 bps margin uplift), translating to a $1.00-$1.20 increase in adjusted EPS, plus $8M-$15M in reduced annual capex.

The closure will result in pretax charges of $227M-$262M through 2029, including $170M-$195M of non-cash charges in Q2/Q3 2026 and $57M-$67M in cash closure costs over three years, partially offset by $15M-$25M in annualized operating capital cash benefits.
Q1 2026 consolidated sales were $455M (flat YoY), with adjusted EBITDA of $49.3M (10.8% margin) versus $56M (12.2%) prior year, and adjusted EPS of $0.57.
Q1 operating cash flow of $46.3M and free cash flow of $34.9M were both first-quarter records, with trailing-12-month operating cash flow of $192M and free cash flow of $139M also at new highs.
Performance Chemicals Q1 sales rose 18% to $142M with EBITDA up to $26M (18% margin), driven by a 15% volume increase including ~9% market share growth and ~6% customer inventory build.

CM&C Q1 sales fell 7% to $93M with EBITDA collapsing to $1M (1% margin) from $10M, as average pricing fell 11% (carbon pitch down 9% globally) amid the lowest quarterly results since the 2016 restructuring began.
RUPS Q1 sales declined to $220M from $235M (with ~$10M from the divested Railroad Structures business) and EBITDA fell to $23M from $26M, though commercial backlog remains strong.

Full-year 2026 guidance was revised: sales maintained at $1.9B-$2.0B, but adjusted EBITDA lowered by $10M to $240M-$260M and adjusted EPS set at $3.80-$4.60, primarily due to a ~$10M unmitigated impact from higher oil prices tied to the Middle East conflict.
